400 series of the census tract area. The 400 series of the census data is in land area several times larger than the Randolph Project. It includes the entire "Fan" district of the city and the Virginia Commonwealth University. The 400 series of the census tract had the highest number of major crimes within the City of Richmond during 1971. The Randolph Project area composed of census tract areas 413, 414, and part of 411, was in the upper one-third of the highest crime rate area. Specifically the Randolph Project area accounted for approximately 700 major crimes during 1971. A majority of these crimes occured within the blighted area (the proposed redevelopment area) of the Randolph Project. In addition census tract area 411, adjacent to the Randolph Project to the north, accounted for 835 major crimes and was the highest crime rate area within the City of Richmond during 1971. These areas mark sharp contrast to census tract area 415, the Maymont Community south of Randolph, where 38 major crimes made it the fourth lowest area within the city during 1971.
